Let me go through each example systematically.

## Example 1 (2025-06-17)

History shows a price channel around 70-75. The model forecasts are generally higher than true outcomes.

Looking at the first few days:
- Model: [74.63, 74.49, 72.58, 72.96, 73.32, 73.67, 71.46, 70.94, 71.38, 69.55, 71.32, 72.93, 73.41, 73.39, 73.30, 72.64, 72.68, 73.12, 73.13, 73.07, 74.14, 74.04, 73.29, 72.82, 73.01, 72.64, 73.16, 75.03, 75.68, 75.44]
- True: [74.64, 74.61, 72.74, 72.97, 73.27, 73.54, 71.15, 70.40, 70.96, 68.97, 70.58, 71.93, 72.06, 71.67, 71.20, 70.42, 70.39, 70.74, 70.55, 70.42, 71.51, 1.31, 70.55, 69.89, 69.83, 69.11, 69.36, 70.88, 71.34, 70.65]

The model is consistently overforecasting by about 0.3-1.0 points in the early days. Looking more closely:


I notice a clear pattern of model overprediction. The initial differences start around 0.3-0.5 points, gradually increasing to 1-2 points by the 6th day. The divergence suggests the model struggles to accurately capture true price movements, particularly in the early days of the forecast.
